questions.question: What structural feature defines a chiral (stereogenic) carbon center in an organic molecule?

options.label: A
options.text: A carbon atom bonded to four identical groups.

options.label: B
options.text: An sp³-hybridized carbon atom bonded to four chemically distinct, non-identical substituents, lacking an internal plane of symmetry.

options.label: C
options.text: Any carbon atom in a cyclic ring.

options.label: D
options.text: An sp²-hybridized planar carbon atom.

questions.correct_answer: An sp³-hybridized carbon atom bonded to four chemically distinct, non-identical substituents, lacking an internal plane of symmetry.
questions.explanation: An sp³ carbon bearing four different groups generates a non-superimposable mirror image (chiral stereocenter).

questions.question: What is the structural relationship between (R)-lactic acid and (S)-lactic acid?

options.label: A
options.text: Constitutional isomers.

options.label: B
options.text: Enantiomers: non-superimposable mirror-image stereoisomers with identical physical properties (bp, mp, density) except for the direction of optical rotation.

options.label: C
options.text: Diastereomers.

options.label: D
options.text: Conformational rotamers.

questions.correct_answer: Enantiomers: non-superimposable mirror-image stereoisomers with identical physical properties (bp, mp, density) except for the direction of optical rotation.
questions.explanation: Enantiomers are exact non-superimposable mirror images that rotate plane-polarized light in equal and opposite directions.

questions.question: How do diastereomers differ fundamentally from enantiomers in their physical properties?

options.label: A
options.text: Diastereomers always have identical melting points.

options.label: B
options.text: Diastereomers cannot be separated by chromatography.

options.label: C
options.text: Diastereomers must rotate polarized light by the exact same angle.

options.label: D
options.text: Diastereomers are stereoisomers that are NOT mirror images; they possess different physical and chemical properties (mp, bp, solubility, NMR spectra).

questions.correct_answer: Diastereomers are stereoisomers that are NOT mirror images; they possess different physical and chemical properties (mp, bp, solubility, NMR spectra).
questions.explanation: Diastereomers are non-mirror-image stereoisomers with different spatial interatomic distances, leading to distinct physical properties.

questions.topic: Meso Compound Criteria and Optical Activity
questions.question: Why is meso-tartaric acid optically inactive ([α] = 0°) despite containing two chiral carbon centers?

options.label: A
options.text: The two chiral centers destroy each other by chemical reaction.

options.label: B
options.text: It contains only sp² carbons.

options.label: C
options.text: It possesses an internal plane of symmetry (or inversion center) that renders the molecule achiral and superimposable on its mirror image.

options.label: D
options.text: It is a 50:50 racemic mixture of two enantiomers.

questions.correct_answer: It possesses an internal plane of symmetry (or inversion center) that renders the molecule achiral and superimposable on its mirror image.
questions.explanation: Meso compounds possess multiple stereocenters but are achiral overall due to an internal symmetry element (mirror plane or center of inversion).

questions.question: According to the Cahn-Ingold-Prelog rules, which group has the highest priority at a chiral center: -OH, -CH₂Br, -CH₂OH, -CH₃?

options.label: A
options.text: -OH has the highest priority because the directly attached atom (oxygen, atomic number 8) has the highest atomic number.

options.label: B
options.text: -CH₂Br because bromine has a higher atomic weight than oxygen.

options.label: C
options.text: -CH₂OH.

options.label: D
options.text: -CH₃.

questions.correct_answer: -OH has the highest priority because the directly attached atom (oxygen, atomic number 8) has the highest atomic number.
questions.explanation: CIP priority is determined strictly by the atomic number of the atom directly attached to the stereocenter (O = 8 vs C = 6).

questions.question: When viewing a stereocenter with the lowest priority group (4) pointing away from the observer, what configuration corresponds to 1 → 2 → 3 clockwise?

options.label: A
options.text: (E) configuration.

options.label: B
options.text: (Z) configuration.

options.label: C
options.text: (S) configuration (sinister, counterclockwise).

options.label: D
options.text: (R) configuration (from Latin rectus, meaning right-handed / clockwise).

questions.correct_answer: (R) configuration (from Latin rectus, meaning right-handed / clockwise).
questions.explanation: Clockwise arrangement of priority groups 1 → 2 → 3 with group 4 pointing away defines the (R) absolute configuration.

questions.question: How is the (E)/(Z) configuration assigned to a tetrasubstituted alkene?

options.label: A
options.text: Assign CIP priorities (1 and 2) to the two groups on each alkene carbon; if the two priority 1 groups are on the same side, it is (Z); if opposite, it is (E).

options.label: B
options.text: Assign based on the boiling point of the alkene.

options.label: C
options.text: Assign based on whether the alkene is cis or trans to hydrogen.

options.label: D
options.text: Assign (Z) if all four groups are identical.

questions.correct_answer: Assign CIP priorities (1 and 2) to the two groups on each alkene carbon; if the two priority 1 groups are on the same side, it is (Z); if opposite, it is (E).
questions.explanation: (Z) (zusammen, together) means high-priority groups on the same side; (E) (entgegen, opposite) means high-priority groups on opposite sides.

questions.topic: Fischer Projection Rules for R/S Assignment
questions.question: When assigning (R) or (S) configuration from a Fischer projection, what rule applies if priority group 4 is on a horizontal bond?

options.label: A
options.text: The result remains unchanged (clockwise = R).

options.label: B
options.text: Group 4 must be deleted before assignment.

options.label: C
options.text: Determine the apparent direction (1 → 2 → 3); because horizontal bonds project forward toward the viewer, reverse the result (clockwise = S, counterclockwise = R).

options.label: D
options.text: Fischer projections cannot be assigned R/S.

questions.correct_answer: Determine the apparent direction (1 → 2 → 3); because horizontal bonds project forward toward the viewer, reverse the result (clockwise = S, counterclockwise = R).
questions.explanation: Horizontal bonds in Fischer projections point toward the viewer; hence, an apparent clockwise trace corresponds to the true (S) configuration.

questions.question: In ethanol (CH₃-CH₂-OH), how are the two methylene hydrogens classified with respect to chirality?

options.label: A
options.text: Enantiotopic: replacing one hydrogen with deuterium creates a chiral center, generating an (R) or (S) enantiomer.

options.label: B
options.text: Constitutional hydrogens.

options.label: C
options.text: Homotopic hydrogens.

options.label: D
options.text: Diastereotopic hydrogens.

questions.correct_answer: Enantiotopic: replacing one hydrogen with deuterium creates a chiral center, generating an (R) or (S) enantiomer.
questions.explanation: The two methylene hydrogens in ethanol reside in enantiotopic environments; replacing one produces a chiral stereocenter (Pro-R vs Pro-S).

options.text: 8 stereoisomers (2³ = 8, consisting of 4 pairs of enantiomers).

options.text: 16 stereoisomers.

options.text: 4 stereoisomers.

questions.explanation: According to the 2^n rule, a molecule with n stereocenters and no symmetry has a maximum of 2^n possible stereoisomers.
